name: HRE EDGE: one lane per municipality, each with its own uplink
info:
Sensors (Python nodes) -> MQTT hre/telemetry/<municipality>/# -> lane: VALIDATE -> EVALUATE -> CLOUD LINK -> database.
Every lane has its own MQTT subscription, validator, fault evaluator, database connection, up/down state and spool folder (~/.node-red/hre-edge/spool/<municipality>/). One municipality losing its uplink never delays another.
The EDGE lane carries province-wide and edge-level events (province outage, edge power).
Settings come from environment variables: PG*, MQTT_HOST/PORT/USER/PASSWORD, EDGE_ID, HRE_DIR, OFFLINE_AFTER_MIN, BATCH_MS. Nothing sensitive is stored in this flow.

info: Faults are injected with the per-VLAN fault scripts (hre_fault_water.py / hre_fault_sewer.py). These buttons clear them and test the validator.

name: LOADSHEDDING: sensors lose power (silent)
info: Retained hre/sim/power/... switches. The Python nodes go quiet; Node-RED must detect it from the silence. Undo with 'Restore ALL power'.

name: UPLINK: per-municipality connectivity to the cloud (sensors keep running)
info: Each lane spools to its own JSON file while its uplink is down and syncs when it returns. 'Loadshed' also logs power_loss / power_restored for that municipality.
